name: croatian_01
context: A tweet in Croatian, posted between April 2013 and February 2015 and collected through the Twitter Search API near the largest cities where the language is spoken. A native speaker labelled each tweet by the emotional attitude of the person who posted it.

versions.analysis_for_next:
Version 0 scored 60.0 macro-F1, and the errors fall into three patterns.

1. Positive is the largest gold class (302 of 600), but 69 positive texts were labelled neutral. Most are dry shared links and announcements: articles, events, festivals, film or celebrity news, tech and game news, recipes, how-to tips, job ads, product launches, check-ins and 'Pročitajte/saznajte' (read/find out) teasers. Annotators treat sharing such content as a positive attitude even with no enthusiasm words.

2. Calls for help are labelled positive, not negative. These include flood-relief appeals, volunteers, 'Dijelite, molim' (please share), anti-racism days and 'ODVEŽITE PSE' (untie the dogs). Annotators read them as solidarity.

3. 54 neutral texts were labelled negative. Many are wry jokes, mild grumbles ('Proljece. Polen. Patim.' = Spring. Pollen. I suffer.), deadpan irony, and political or economic commentary or statistics without strong anger. Annotators keep negative for clear hostility, insults, sadness, explicit hate or clearly tragic news.

Neutral texts labelled positive (41) are casual chat with smileys, sports chants, and promos read as enthusiastic. Some of these look like annotator noise, so I will not chase them hard.

Changes for version 1:
- Make positive the default for shared content on cultural, lifestyle, tech, entertainment, business and help topics.
- Narrow negative to explicit hostility, distress or clearly bad events.
- Keep neutral for chat replies, plain personal remarks, dry irony, mild complaints, and political or economic news and statistics.
- Keep negative cues strong so negative recall stays high.

Version 1 overcorrected and fell to 50.1 macro-F1.

What went wrong:
- Negative recall collapsed from 135 to 35 of 155 negative texts. 90 negative texts went to neutral: mild complaints (rain, flu, mosquitoes, low pay), wry or sarcastic jokes, ironic remarks, and dry headlines about bad economic or political news (record debt, GDP fall, Crimea tensions, government failures). These annotators do treat mild grumbles, irony and bad-news headlines as negative, as version 0 assumed.
- Making positive the default for all shared content pulled 79 neutral texts into positive. These were political, business and sports news, statistics, line-ups, horoscopes, cooking facts, church readings and plain check-ins.

What improved and should stay:
- Positive recall rose from 201 to 264. Cultural, entertainment and lifestyle shares and help appeals should stay positive.

Plan for version 2:
- Restore the version 0 negative criteria: complaints, irony, sarcasm, mockery, frustration and bad-news headlines count as negative even when mild or joking.
- Keep positive for event, culture, film and celebrity shares, tech and game news, recipes and how-to tips, job ads, product launches, help or volunteer appeals, friendly warm replies and nice check-ins.
- Keep neutral for politics, business, economy and sports news with no clear good or bad slant, and for statistics, line-ups, plain questions, logistics chat and plain statements.

Version 3 was 407 words, over the 400-word limit, so I trimmed it without changing its approach.

The approach stays the same. Neutral recall was very low (26 of 143). The neutral texts labelled negative are mostly deadpan observations with no target, calm opinions or statistics, and banter. The negative texts that version 1 lost were the poster's own complaints, sarcasm with a target, and bad-news headlines.

So version 3 keeps negative for being bothered or attacking, and moves untargeted wit and calm analysis to neutral. Positive stays as in version 2.

To cut the word count I removed one long neutral example and shortened some descriptions and cues.

Version 4 is the best so far at 63.5 macro-F1, but positive texts labelled neutral rose from 30 to 36.

What moved positive texts to neutral:
- Moving bare product names and specs to neutral pulled in commercial listings that annotators label positive. These include accommodation ads ('Apartments Batur - Zadar - Croatia'), shop offers (backpacks, honey products), cooking tips (#321kuhaj), article teasers ('Pitanje za milijun dolara!', 'Kako povezati znanost i gospodarstvo?') and city check-ins.
- So promotional listings, tips and teasers should be positive. Only political or institutional events, religious texts and horoscopes stay neutral.

Negative texts labelled neutral are partly political news that report criticism, accusations, fear or legal action ('Putin žestoko kritizira', 'Turudić: Ministar nije u pravu', 'Josipović: Plaši me', '#AZTN pokrenuo postupak'). I will add criticism, accusations, threats and legal proceedings to the bad-news part of negative.

The neutral texts mislabelled as positive or negative are still largely friendly chat with smileys and deadpan humour. The labels there are noisy, so I keep that boundary as in version 4.

The edits are small and the question stays under 400 words.

Version 6 was 402 words, just over the limit, so I trimmed a few words from the rule and cues without changing the content.

The change from version 5 stays: casual @reply chat where a smiley is the only positive sign is neutral, not positive. Sports chants, dividends and nutrition facts are also added to neutral. Everything else is as in version 5.

versions.analysis_for_next:
Version 7 was 408 words, over the 400-word limit. I trimmed it by removing one positive example and shortening the rule and descriptions; the content is unchanged.

The approach stays the same: @replies are split by their main content. Friendly ones (invitations, agreement, encouragement, greetings, cheering, playful laughter) are positive. Informational, logistical or opinion replies are neutral even with a smiley. Article teasers stay positive. Negative is unchanged.

versions.analysis_for_next:
Version 8 was 408 words, over the 400-word limit. I removed one positive example and shortened the rule and descriptions; the content is unchanged.

Version 8 is version 6 plus one fix: good news in economy or politics (growth, recovery, profit, records, success) counts as positive. Replies keep the version 6 rule that a smiley alone does not make them positive.

versions.analysis_for_next:
Versions 5 to 8 all score 63 to 65 macro-F1. Version 6 is the best at 65.1, and the differences between versions are largely within noise. Many of the remaining errors are inconsistent gold labels: near-identical friendly replies, flood-help posts, check-ins and cooking tips carry different labels.

Version 8's 'good news is positive' clause pushed borderline neutral news ('Novi zakon prihvatljiv LGBT', 'Drogba... pobjednike') to positive. It also failed to rescue most of the target texts, so the net effect was negative.

Version 9 therefore goes back to version 6, with one small cue change. I swap two weak positive cues for 'kako' (how to) and 'rekord' (record), so how-to teasers and record news lean positive.

Everything else stays as in version 6:
- the rule that a smiley alone does not make an @reply positive;
- the neutral bucket for political events, statistics, religious texts and horoscopes;
- the negative definition built on the poster being bothered or attacking.

versions.analysis_for_next:
Version 10 was 415 words, over the 400-word limit. I removed one positive example and shortened the rule and descriptions; the content is unchanged.

The final version keeps version 9, with one narrow change. @replies count as positive only when they contain a greeting, an invitation, encouragement or cheering. Laughter, agreement and informational replies with smileys stay neutral.
